title: Online vs. In-Person Therapy: Which Is Better?
description: Comparing teletherapy and traditional in-office therapy. What research shows about effectiveness, who each format works best for, and how to decide.

content.text: Since the pandemic, online therapy has become mainstream. But is it as effective as sitting in a therapist's office? Here's what the research shows.
A 2021 meta-analysis found video-based therapy was equally effective to in-person therapy for depression and anxiety, with similar dropout rates and therapeutic alliance.
For most common conditions (depression, anxiety, PTSD), teletherapy produces equivalent outcomes to in-person treatment.

items: Access to specialists regardless of location
Easier for social anxiety or agoraphobia
Some techniques require presence (EMDR with tactile stimulation)
What's your comfort level with technology?
Do you have reliable internet and private space?
Would commuting be a barrier to consistent attendance?
Does your condition require in-person care?

content.text: Many people do hybrid—some sessions online, some in-person. This offers flexibility while maintaining the option for in-person when needed.

For most people with depression or anxiety, online therapy works as well as in-person. The best therapy is the one you'll actually attend. If online removes barriers, it's the better choice. If you crave the ritual of leaving home and being in a dedicated space, in-person may suit you better.
